content:
Hi everyone,

Happy to announce VCVio, a library for formally verified cryptographic proofs!

The library has been around for a while, and is now ready for a broad announcement. We also released a companion paper (https://eprint.iacr.org/2026/899) describing our approach. This is joint work with @Devon Tuma, @Alexander Hicks, James Waters, and Nicholas Hopper.

VCVio's main objects (oracle computations, oracle behaviors) are a direct implementation of algebraic effects & handlers, on top of free monads on polynomial functors. This makes standard cryptographic manipulations manipulations like query logging, replay, programming, etc. part of a composable handler system.

This design choice allows us to build directly on polynomial functors (PFunctor in mathlib). In fact, we have separated out the (substantial) development of PFunctor into a new library PolyFun, which may be of independent interest (we do not bake in any cryptographic notions). It is well known that polynomial functors can be used to model interactive systems (https://toposinstitute.github.io/poly/poly-book.pdf), and PolyFun hopes to provide such a framework.

We also implemented a modular relational program logic for probabilistic and expectation-based reasoning, building upon Loom and eRHL. Our tactics framework build directly on loom2 and mvcgen, though much work on this remains to be done. We also offer a state separating proof (SSP) layer, which we interpret in our library to simply be stateful handlers and composition operators for them.

There has been some discussion of VCVio in the CSLib channel, and some comparison with a (yet to be publicly released) CatCrypt library by @Bas Spitters . We are interested in upstreaming shared preliminaries to CSLib to help with projects like Signal Shot.
